annotations.text: Now: the card always fills the room, so a short reply hangs under an empty block.
A: the card is as tall as the words; the free room is plain background. Calm, but the trackpad shrinks with the text, and a long reply is cut at the top again.
B: the blank top shows what the turn did: done/time, diff, commit, release. Useful, but only when the turn did something.
C: words start at the top, a short reply set larger. Reads like a note, but a long one still has to be cut.

D (recommended): the end of the chat, as on the Mac: your message, the steps, the reply. Short reply → earlier turns fill the room; the pad scrolls the Mac and the card looks like what it scrolls. Empty only when the whole thread is that short.

E1 (recommended): the chat is a dark recessed screen with ON THE MAC and a position rail. Reads as a window onto the computer, not a list in the phone; the dark glass is the 'not here' signal. Matches the Mac's own dark chat.
E2: a matte, dotted, sunken surface over the chat, like a trackpad you touch through. Says 'drag here', but the dot grid sits on top of the words and costs a bit of legibility.

E3: the chat stays plain; a ribbed wheel on the edge is the control and its knob shows where the Mac is in the chat. Clearest 'this is a control', but it looks like the wheel is the only place to drag.

F1 (recommended): E1's dark screen with E2's dots, light and faint on the dark glass, like a speaker grille or an LED panel. Words stay crisp; the dots alone say 'surface you drag', the dark says 'that's the Mac'.
F2: E2 kept light, without the blur. Dots are dense on top where older turns fade out and thin under the newest words, so the reply reads clean. ON THE MAC and the position rail from E1.
